decisions.question: S37 found that ADR-002 item 4's rule (a third-party caret constraint's lower bound is the version the committed lockfile resolves when the dependency is added) produces constraints that cannot resolve: nidana.model.1 runs with no Flutter member, resolves test 1.33.0 and writes test: ^1.33.0, which beside a Flutter member does not resolve (flutter_test holds test at 1.31.1), so nidana.flutter.1's pub get fails; analyzer ^14.5.0 fails the same way against the plugin's 13.3.0 pin. Fix it now with an hsdd-adr step before nidana.tooling.codegen's plan, or carry it to the stage-7 pass?

options.label: Amend ADR-002 now, before codegen's plan
options.consequence: One hsdd-adr step; codegen's plan (which creates a member) and integration's plan are written against a rule that resolves; the member-creating phase scopes already written by model, runtime, navigation, flutter and lint are updated to match in the stage-7 pass, as hsdd-reconcile updates scopes that assumed otherwise.

options.label: Carry it to stage 7
options.consequence: Two more plans would copy the broken rule into their scopes, widening the later sweep.

decisions.chosen: Amend ADR-002 now, before codegen's plan
decisions.why: This is a defect in an accepted decision, demonstrated by experiment (docs/auto-run/experiments/lint-reconcile-amends/constraints.sh, K1 to K6), and it would make the first Flutter phase fail at pub get. The policy has the run write and accept ADRs, so amending one is within it; it is not a run-stop. Fixing the rule before the remaining two plans keeps them from repeating it.
